answer: The verifier mandates 1,000 unique location proofs per agent to anchor identity on a digital map. Each unit must complete physical signal triangulation at a specific lagoon of base stations; an honest participant pays linear costs for travel, while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes faces extreme spatial congestion. The system measures the delta in signal arrival time to generate an umber-tinted pigment pattern in the audit log, acting as falsifiable evidence. If a relay detects overlapping pulses, it immediately invalidates the identity, ensuring uniqueness for every autonomous node.
